svg.title: Reading an Effect Size
svg.desc: Three pairs of overlapping bell curves on the same axes. Small: d = 0.2, the treatment curve sits just to the right of the control curve and almost all of it overlaps. Medium: d = 0.5, the curves are clearly offset with a large overlap. Large: d = 0.8, the curves are further apart with less overlap. Under the curves the formula reads d = (mean of treatment minus mean of control) / pooled standard deviation. A caution strip says the pilot difference of 7.0 over a pooled standard deviation of about 6.78 gives d of about 1.03, from only 12 students per group, which deserves a second look.
svg.text: The more the two curves separate, the larger d. Same axes in every panel.

d = (mean of treatment − mean of control) / pooled standard deviation
Caution: a big number from a small test
The Watershed Basics pilot: a difference of 7.0 over a pooled standard deviation of about 6.78 gives d of about 1.03. With only 12
students per group, an impressive estimate often shrinks when the test is repeated with more students.
